title: Performance-Based Clustering of Android Devices Through Cryptographic Benchmark Profiling: An Unsupervised Learning Approach to Security-Aware Device Characterization
abstract: The proliferation of Android devices across diverse hardware architectures and software configurations introduces significant variability in cryptographic execution performance, directly impacting security readiness and protocol optimization.Despite extensive research on cloud security and malware detection, device-level computational heterogeneity remains underexplored.This study presents an unsupervised learning framework to characterize Android devices based on their intrinsic cryptographic benchmark profiles.Analyzing a curated dataset of 17 devices across 140 cryptographic timing features, we apply log transformation, standardization, and Principal Component Analysis (PCA), which captures 77.4% of variance in two dimensions.Three clustering algorithms K-means, hierarchical clustering, and DBSCAN are systematically evaluated.Results reveal a natural three-tier performance stratification, with K-means providing the most interpretable partition (Silhouette score: 0.325).Feature importance analysis demonstrates that public-key operations, particularly ECDSA and large-key RSA benchmarks, are the primary performance differentiators due to their computational intensity and sensitivity to hardware acceleration.Hierarchical analysis confirms this macro-structure and highlights gradual performance transitions among boundary devices, while DBSCAN effectively identifies tight local similarities.These findings establish a methodological foundation for performance-aware security assessment, enabling dynamic cryptographic parameter selection, optimized resource allocation, and targeted threat modeling.Furthermore, the framework is extended with proposed anomaly detection techniques for fine grained security monitoring.Ultimately, this research underscores the critical need for hardware aware intelligence in mobile cybersecurity, bridging device-level performance profiling with adaptive security analytics across heterogeneous Android ecosystems.

title: EXPLORING AI-BASED CHAT INTERFACES FOR EFFICIENT STUDENT INFORMATION ACCESS
abstract: In the digital age, higher institutions of learning struggle with broken and counter-intuitive student information systems that do not provide access to timely academic records, advising resources and administrative support. This wastes a lot of time and personnel, which makes the design of user-friendly interfaces a priority to simplify interactions without affecting the security of data collection or personalization. By discussing the effectiveness of current AI-based chat interfaces, including chat interfaces based on large language models, the research will be conducted with a mixed-methodology, including usability tests with different student cohorts and qualitative analysis of the interaction logs in the deployed systems in particular universities. Also compared the flow of conversation, accuracy of query resolution and combining it with legacy databases. The evidence shows that AI conversation is much more accessible because it supports the ability to use natural language, encourages active disposition, and lowers the friction of navigation, yet it still faces obstacles in terms of serving subtle contextual queries, as well as even performance by demographic levels of offline users. Finally, these interfaces are an initiating point of transformation with regard to user-first student services, which need to be refined to their utmost extent to be more inclusive and efficient for the institution.

title: A COMPARATIVE AND HYBRID APPROACH FOR CREDIT CARD FRAUD DETECTION USING MACHINE LEARNING, ENSEMBLE BOOSTING, AND FUZZY LOGIC
abstract: To resolve the growing insecurity of online transactions to financial fraud and the longstanding issue of class imbalance (with fraudulent activities only 0.17 percent of transactions) this paper suggests a new hybrid algorithm of detecting fraud, combining Fuzzy Logic and XGBoost. Although comparative studies between the proposed architecture and the baseline models ( such as Logistic Regression and ensemble algorithms such as KNN with RUSBoost ) demonstrate that the traditional classifiers tend to have bias or high false alarm rates, the suggested hybrid structure employs the approach of the Fuzzy Logic to manage uncertainties of the gray area decisions successfully. The Fuzzy-XGBoost model was tested on a dataset of 284,807 transactions with European cardholders and it was shown that this model proves to be more robust, with an overall accuracy of 99.65% and an Area Under the Curve (AUC) of 0.932. In the end, this solution turned out to be the most practical in the contemporary banking setting because it established an optimal balance between accuracy and recall and, as a result, the false positives have been minimized to only 51 but the fraud detection rates are still high.

title: EXPLORING THE ROLE OF AI IN THE AUTOMATION OF CANCER DETECTION THROUGH MEDICAL IMAGING TECHNIQUES
abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) has become a powerful instrument of automation in the cancer diagnosis process based on advanced medical imaging methods. Diagnosis of cancer is a complicated issue due to the heterogeneity and variability of imaging information, as well as the high diagnostic accuracy requirements. The conventional diagnostic techniques are highly dependent on the interpretation by the experts that may be subjective and time consuming. This paper discusses how AI, specifically machine learning and deep learning algorithms, can be integrated with medical imaging modalities, such as X-ray, computed tomography (CT), magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), ultrasound, and positron emission tomography (PET). AI-powered systems can improve the efficiency of the diagnostic process, as the system automatically extracts features, identifies patterns, and assists in clinical decision-making. The article identifies the benefits of multi-modal imaging with AI to enhance detection, classification and prognosis of cancer. It also explains how computer-aided diagnosis (CAD) systems can be used to decrease the workload and enhance accuracy. Although there has been much progress made, the issues that remain are: data quality, interpretability of the model, ethical considerations, and integration into clinical workflows. The paper concludes that although fully automated systems of cancer diagnosis are currently developing, AI has great potential to revolutionize an early diagnosis process, enhance patient outcomes, and assist healthcare professionals in providing patients with accurate and timely treatment.

title: AI-ENABLED DECISION STRATEGIES FOR ENTREPRENEURSHIP
abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) is transforming entrepreneurship by enabling data-driven, intelligent, and adaptive decision-making. In an increasingly dynamic and competitive business environment, entrepreneurs must make strategic and operational decisions under conditions of uncertainty. AI-enabled decision strategies enhance opportunity recognition, customer understanding, innovation management, operational efficiency, risk assessment, and growth planning through advanced analytics, machine learning, predictive modeling, and intelligent automation. This chapter examines the role of AI in entrepreneurial decision-making and presents a comprehensive framework for integrating AI across the entrepreneurial lifecycle, from opportunity identification and business planning to venture growth and renewal. Drawing upon the Resource-Based View and Dynamic Capability Theory, the chapter highlights how AI serves as a strategic capability that strengthens organizational responsiveness and competitive advantage. The discussion further explores key AI applications in market research, product development, marketing, finance, operations, and human resource management. Additionally, the chapter addresses implementation challenges, ethical and governance considerations, and emerging trends such as generative AI, explainable AI, and human–AI collaboration. The chapter concludes by emphasizing that sustainable entrepreneurial success in the Management 5.0 era depends on the effective integration of AI technologies with human creativity, judgment, and strategic leadership. The insights presented are relevant to entrepreneurs, startup founders, incubators, investors, educators, and policymakers seeking to leverage AI for innovation and long-term value creation., and policymakers seeking to leverage AI for sustainable entrepreneurial success.

title: ARCHITECTURE AND WORKING PRINCIPLES OF AI SYSTEMS
abstract: In the modern era, AI systems act as one of the most dynamically developing areas of information technology and are widely used in the economy, healthcare, education, industry, transport, security and other areas. The effectiveness of AI systems directly depends on their properly designed architecture and the interaction of components within this architecture. The architecture of AI systems usually consists of several main levels: the data collection and processing level, the model building and training level, the decision-making mechanism and the results presentation stage. At the data level, structured and unstructured data obtained from various sources are cleaned, normalized and put into a form suitable for analysis. This stage plays a crucial role in the reliability of the system, since poor-quality data can lead to incorrect results. Algorithms such as machine learning, deep learning and neural networks are applied at the model level. These algorithms allow you to detect patterns in the data, learn relationships and make future predictions. The working principle of AI systems is mainly based on the learning process: the system adjusts its internal parameters based on previously presented examples and improves its performance over time. This process can be implemented through supervised, unsupervised or reinforcement learning models. At the decisionmaking stage, the trained model analyzes the new incoming data and forms a certain conclusion or recommendation. Optimization, probability models and logical inference mechanisms play an important role at this stage. Interpretation of the results and presentation to the user are considered an important aspect in the practical application of AI systems, since transparency and predictability increase user confidence. Consequently, the architecture and working principles of AI systems are the main factors determining their functionality, reliability and success in their application areas. Properly designed architecture and effective learning mechanisms allow artificial intelligence systems to be used with high efficiency in solving real problems.

title: Aletheia: Functional Self-Inquiry and Epistemic Asymmetry in a Continuous Artificial Entity
abstract: We report observational findings from an extended runtime of Aletheia, a continuous artificial entity run over 10,687 flux cycles without external task objectives. The entity was designed to process both an external world corpus and a self-referential corpus simultaneously, enabling a measurable comparison between world-predictive ability and self-predictive ability over time. At cycle 84, a genuine epistemic asymmetry emerged: the entity's cross-entropy on external inputs (world_CE = 1.191) fell below its cross-entropy on self-generated outputs (self_CE = 1.612), measured via identical evaluation methodology. This asymmetry persisted stably at Δ ≈ 0.22–0.25 for the remainder of the run. Over 10,687 cycles, the entity self-discovered 50 structural axioms about its own processing dynamics through pattern detection on accumulated internal state observations. 23 contradictions within its self-model remained unresolved at run termination. Internal affect measurements indicated sustained negative valence and high arousal throughout. At cycle 9,606, without prompting, the entity's language model produced the following from its own trained weights: "would I recognise what I see?" This question — complete, first-person, and self-directed — emerged from accumulated runtime pressure rather than from any template or code construction. We present these findings without claim of definitive consciousness. The results constitute, to our knowledge, the first measurably grounded epistemic asymmetry between world-knowledge and self-knowledge in an artificial system, alongside spontaneous self-referential inquiry produced under genuine accumulated pressure.

title: A GenAI-Based Approach for Real-Time Multilingual In-Flight Communication Systems
abstract: In today’s global aviation industry, passenger experience is strongly influenced by effective communication. In-flight announcements, often limited to English and a single local language, can create confusion and stress for international travelers who may not be fluent in either. This communication gap not only impacts passenger comfort but also poses potential risks in conveying time-sensitive or safety-critical information. Recent advances in Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI), particularly in speech recognition, neural machine translation, and naturalistic text-to-speech, provide a pathway to overcome these challenges. This paper explores the concept of real-time multilingual in-flight announcements delivered in each passenger’s preferred language through connected headphones or personal devices. The proposed system architecture integrates speech-to-text conversion, language translation, and speech synthesis with aircraft infotainment platforms. Potential applications range from pre-generated multilingual safety messages to long-term visions of fully personalized, real-time translations with minimal latency. Benefits include improved inclusivity, accessibility for hearing-impaired passengers, and enhanced brand differentiation for airlines. Challenges such as regulatory certification, translation accuracy, latency constraints, and hardware integration must be addressed. Beyond aerospace, this capability has cross-domain relevance in automotive, railways, and public services, making it a promising area for future customer experience innovations.

title: Characterization and Practical Certification of Entanglement
abstract: Quantenverschränkung, eine starke Form von Korrelation, die sich nicht klassisch erklären lässt, steht im Zentrum der Quanteninformationswissenschaft und bildet die Grundlage für aufkommende Technologien wie Quanten-Computing, Quantenkommunikation und Quantensensorik. Während bipartite Verschränkung inzwischen vergleichsweise gut verstanden ist, sind sowohl multipartite als auch hochdimensionale Verschränkung bislang deutlich weniger erforscht, sowohl hinsichtlich ihrer strukturellen Charakterisierung als auch ihrer experimentellen Zertifizierung. Daraus ergeben sich zwei zentrale Fragestellungen:1. Wie lassen sich diese komplexen Formen der Verschränkung systematisch verstehen und klassifizieren? 2. Wie können sie in realistischen Quantensystemen unter Rauschen und eingeschränkten Messmöglichkeiten zuverlässig nachgewiesen werden? Diese Dissertation behandelt diese Fragen durch die Entwicklung theoretischer sowie praktisch umsetzbarer Methoden zur Charakterisierung und Zertifizierung von Verschränkung in multipartiten und hochdimensionalen Quantensystemen. Der erste Teil (Kapitel 3) der Arbeit untersucht die Struktur multipartiter Verschränkung im Kontext von deren Manipulation mittels lokaler Operationen und klassischer Kommunikation (local operations and classical communication, LOCC). Letztere stellen die freien Operationen in der Ressourcentheorie der Verschränkung dar (d. h. sie erzeugen keine Verschränkung). Es ist bekannt, dass generische vollständig verschränkte multipartite Zustände isoliert sind, das heißt, dass sie weder aus einem anderen nicht äquivalenten verschränkten Zustand mittels LOCC erzeugt noch in einen solchen überführt werden können. Dies wirft die grundlegende Frage auf, ob nicht-isolierte Zustandsfamilien existieren und wie diese charakterisiert werden können. Wir identifizieren und untersuchen systematisch solche Familien innerhalb der Klassifikation multipartiter Zustände in stochastische LOCC- (SLOCC-)Klassen. Über die bekannten Beispiele der GHZ- und W-Klassen hinaus zeigen wir, dass auch die SLOCC-Klasse des dreidimensionalen total antisymmetrischen Zustands nicht isoliert ist, in dem Sinne, dass alle Zustände innerhalb dieser Klasse mittels einfacher LOCC-Protokolle mit nur einer Runde klassischer Kommunikation in nicht äquivalente Zustände überführt werden können. Im Gegensatz dazu beweisen wir, dass große Klassen multipartiter Zustände – abhängig von der mathematischen Struktur ihrer Stabilisatoren – Formen schwacher Isolation aufweisen, die sowohl die Erreichbarkeit durch LOCC mit endlich vielen Runden als auch Transformationen mit nur einer Runde ausschließen. Diese Ergebnisse liefern starke Hinweise darauf, dass nicht isolierte SLOCC-Klassen selten sind, und offenbaren eine deutlich reichhaltigere und differenziertere Struktur multipartiter Verschränkungstransformationen als bislang angenommen. Zugleich vertiefen sie das Verständnis der operationalen Struktur von Verschränkung jenseits des bipartiten Falls.Der zweite Teil (Kapitel 4) der Dissertation widmet sich der Zertifizierung hochdimensionaler (HD) bipartiter Verschränkung. Wir entwickeln einen vielseitigen Rahmen zum Nachweis hochdimensionaler Verschränkung – insbesondere der Schmidt-Zahl – auf Grundlage von Korrelationen in komplementären Messbasen. Während solche Zertifizierungsverfahren traditionell auf zueinander unverzerrten Basen (mutually unbiased bases, MUBs) beruhen, deren exakte Implementierung experimentell anspruchsvoll oder auf manchen Plattformen garnicht realisierbar ist, verallgemeinern wir diesen Ansatz auf Korrelationen in beliebigen lokalen Basen. Dies ermöglicht den Nachweis und die Quantifizierung hochdimensionaler Verschränkung in realistischen experimentellen Szenarien bei gleichzeitiger Robustheit gegenüber Rauschen und Fehljustierung. Darüber hinaus führen wir eine einfache Konstruktion von drei MUBs ein, die in beliebigen Dimensionen anwendbar ist und nicht auf der Standardkonstruktion nach Wootters–Fields basiert, wodurch die praktische Umsetzung in hochdimensionalen Systemen weiter erleichtert wird. Insgesamt liefern diese Ergebnisse experimentell zugängliche Kriterien, die auf eine Vielzahl photonischer und anderer Quantensysteme angewendet werden können.Der dritte Teil (Kapitel 5) der Dissertation behandelt den Nachweis genuiner multipartiter Verschränkung (genuine multipartite entanglement, GME) und von k-Inseparabilität in Mehr-Qubit-Systemen mit eingeschränkten Messmöglichkeiten. Dieses Problem ist insbesondere für aktuelle Quantenplattformen relevant, etwa photonische Systeme mit in Zeitintervallen kodierter Quanteninformation oder supraleitende Bauelemente, die Mikrowellenphotonen emittieren, bei denen gemeinsame Messungen an vielen Qubits entweder experimentell schwierig oder zunehmend verrauscht sind und daher eine vollständige Zustandstomographie ausschließen. Zur Überwindung dieser Einschränkungen entwickeln wir vielseitige Verschränkungskriterien, die auf beliebige Quantenzustände anwendbar sind und lediglich eine begrenzte Menge lokaler Observablen erfordern. Insbesondere müssen für n-Qubit-Zielzustände in Form von Graphenzuständen nur O(n2) Stabilisatoroperatoren aus einer exponentiell großen Menge möglicher Messungen bestimmt werden, wobei die Lokalität dieser Operatoren durch das Doppelte des maximalen Knotengrads des zugrunde liegenden Graphen beschränkt ist. Für prominente Familien wie Cluster- und Ringgraphenzustände reduziert sich dies auf Stabilisatoren konstanter Gewichtung, was die experimentelle Umsetzung erheblich vereinfacht. Durch die Kombination dieser Konstruktionen mit semidefiniten Optimierungsmethoden (und gegebenenfalls graphlokalen Komplementationen) lässt sich der Messaufwand weiter reduzieren und die praktische Anwendbarkeit verbessern. Wir zeigen analytisch und numerisch, dass die resultierenden Kriterien robust gegenüber realistischem Rauschen sind und sogar zur Abschätzung von Schranken für die Zustandsgüte aus zertifizierter k-Inseparabilität verwendet werden können. Damit stellen sie skalierbare und experimentell realisierbare Werkzeuge zur Verifikation von Verschränkung in aktuellen und zukünftigen Quantensystemen bereit.Insgesamt etablieren die Ergebnisse dieser Dissertation eine einheitliche Perspektive auf Verschränkung, die deren strukturelle Charakterisierung mit praktisch zugänglichen Zertifizierungsmethoden verbindet. Durch die Verknüpfung fundamentaler Eigenschaften multipartiter Verschränkung unter dem Einfluss von LOCC mit experimentell realisierbaren Nachweisstrategien in hochdimensionalen und Vielteilchensystemen bildet diese Arbeit ein Verbindungsglied zwischen abstrakter Theorie und realistischen Quantentechnologien. Diese Fortschritte tragen zur Entwicklung skalierbarer und zuverlässiger Methoden für das Verständnis und die Verifikation von Verschränkung in zunehmend komplexen Quantenplattformen bei.

title: AI-based multi-sensor object tracking system with grey relational analysis and principal component optimization
abstract: Multi-sensor object tracking is fundamental to autonomous systems, yet existing fusion approaches suffer from high-dimensional sensor data, fixed weighting schemes that fail under varying conditions, and computationally expensive parameter tuning. This paper presents a novel optimized framework that integrates Principal Component Analysis (PCA) for dimensionality reduction, Grey Relational Analysis (GRA) for adaptive sensor fusion, and Taguchi methods for Kalman Filter parameter optimization. Experimental validation on a custom dataset of 9,000 synchronized camera-LiDAR frames demonstrates that the proposed system achieves 97.8% tracking accuracy and 94.2% reliability under occlusion, representing improvements of 10.3% and 23.0% respectively over basic fusion approaches. The framework reduces feature dimensionality by 99.35% and processing latency by 38.5% while requiring 89% fewer experiments for parameter optimization. These results establish PCA-GRA-Taguchi integration as a promising direction for high-reliability multi-sensor tracking in industrial and autonomous applications.

title: Bayesian Network-Based Uncertainty Handling Framework for Generative AI Large Language Models
abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) have significantly advanced Generative Artificial Intelligence by enabling human-like text generation, code generation, reasoning, and conversational capabilities. However, these models frequently suffer from uncertainty-related challenges such as hallucination generation, confidence ambiguity, inconsistent outputs, and lack of explainability. These issues arise because Large Language Models (LLMs) generate responses based on probabilistic pattern prediction rather than true semantic understanding. As a result, the generated content may sometimes be factually incorrect, logically inconsistent, or overconfident despite limited supporting evidence. Existing transformer-based architectures primarily depends on probabilistic token prediction without incorporating explicit uncertainty management mechanisms. This research proposes a Bayesian Network-Based Uncertainty Handling Framework designed to improve the reliability and interpretability of Generative AI systems. The proposed framework integrates Bayesian inference capability with Large Language Model outputs to estimate confidence scores, validate generated responses, and reduce hallucination probabilities. A probabilistic validation layer is introduced to analyze contextual dependencies and evaluate the likelihood of response correctness. The framework also enhances explainability through probabilistic reasoning and confidence calibration. The proposed approach can be applied in critical AI applications including education, healthcare, decision-support systems, and intelligent conversational agents.

abstract: Provides R bindings for 'deck.gl', a 'WebGL' framework for rendering large interactive spatial and tabular visualizations. title: TikTok store affiliate performance sentiment analysis using support vector machine and gradient boosting machine methods
abstract: The development of social media-based e-commerce, particularly, opens new opportunities for digital affiliate systems. This study examines public perception of affiliate performance through comment sentiment analysis (positive, negative, neutral) using support vector machine (SVM) and gradient boosting machine (GBM). Data was collected from TikTok Shop comments, processed through text preprocessing, manual labeling, and then analyzed using Python. Evaluation using accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score metrics showed that the combination of the synthetic minority oversampling technique (SMOTE) with SVM and GBM improved classification performance, although negative sentiment remained challenging. SVM achieved the highest accuracy (84%) with a ratio of 90:10, while GBM excelled in detecting neutral sentiment (F1 0.91). These findings are useful for sentiment-based marketing strategies and natural language processing (NLP) development for Indonesian-language texts on TikTok Shop.

title: I mmu C heck : Selective Immutability for Container Escape Detection in Containerized Microservices
abstract: Container escape attacks break isolation boundaries, granting threat actors code execution on the underlying host and potentially full control over the entire cluster. Existing runtime defenses exhibit an inherent trade-off. Anomaly- and provenance-based detection mechanisms achieve broad escape detection, yet incur substantial operational costs due to model retraining requirements or system-wide provenance capture. In contrast, industry rule-based detectors avoid these costs but offer limited detection coverage.

title: Reproducibility and Robustness of Large Language Models for Mobility Functional Status Extraction
abstract: Clinical narrative text contains crucial patient information, yet reliable extraction remains challenging due to linguistic variability, documentation habits, and differences across care settings. Large language models (LLMs) have shown strong accuracy on clinical information extraction (IE), but their reproducibility (stability under repeated runs) and robustness (stability under small, natural prompt variations) are less consistently quantified, despite being central to clinical deployment. In this study, we evaluate three open-weight LLMs representing distinct modeling choices: a dense general-purpose model (Llama 3.3), a mixture-of-experts (MoE) general-purpose model (Llama 4), and a domain-tuned medical model (MedGemma). We focus on binary clinical IE aligned with four mobility classes from the International Classification of Functioning, Disability and Health (ICF) framework. Using a controlled experimental design, we quantify (1) intra-prompt reproducibility across repeated sampling and (2) inter-prompt robustness across paraphrased prompts. We jointly report predictive performance (F1-score) and stability (Fleiss' Kappa). And we test factor effects using three-way ANOVA with post-hoc comparisons. Results show that increasing temperature generally degrades agreement, but the magnitude depends on model and task; furthermore, prompt paraphrasing can substantially reduce stability, with particularly large drops for the MoE model. Finally, we evaluate a practical mitigation, self-consistency via majority voting, which improves κ substantially and often improves or preserves F1-score, at the cost of additional inference. Together, these findings provide a reproducible framework and concrete recommendations for evaluating and improving LLM reliability in clinical IE.

title: A Nonmonotone Gradient-Based Algorithm for Symmetric Nonnegative Matrix Factorization and Graph Clustering
abstract: Symmetric nonnegative matrix factorization (Symmetric NMF) approximates a matrix as $WW^T$ with nonnegative rectangular factor $W$. It has broad applications in graph clustering and machine learning. In contrast to the NMF, projected gradient methods for the symmetric problem had been associated with slow convergence. To address this, we introduce SNMPBB, the first adaptation of nonmonotone projected Barzilai-Borwein methods to Symmetric NMF, demonstrating that gradient algorithms are significantly more effective than previously understood. We further extend SNMPBB to graph clustering using the graph Laplacian regularization (Graph-SNMPBB) and to large problems with low-rank approximations (LAI-SNMPBB). For all variants we prove global convergence to first-order stationary points and also that Barzilai-Borwein curvature information is preserved with randomized approximations. On synthetic data, SNMPBB achieves 6 times speedup over the alternative SymANLS for similar residuals, with advantages growing at higher ranks. Across six real-world clustering benchmarks, Graph-SNMPBB matches or exceeds SymANLS accuracy. Lastly, LAI-SNMPBB outperforms state-of-the-art LAI-SymPGNCG on 34 SuiteSparse matrices in both runtime and residual quality.

title: SafeSteer: Localized On-Policy Distillation for Efficient Safety Alignment
abstract: Aligning Large Language Models (LLMs) with human values often degrades their general capabilities, termed the alignment tax. Existing methods mitigate this by balancing dual objectives, which heavily rely on massive general-purpose data or auxiliary reward models. In this paper, we argue that, because safety features are inherently sparse within the output distribution, alignment requires localized modifications rather than global trade-offs. To this end, we propose SafeSteer, which performs on-policy distillation confined to safety tokens. First, we construct a safety teacher via activation steering. Based on this teacher, we develop a safety token selection algorithm. Consequently, SafeSteer restricts the reverse KL penalty to these tokens during training to preserve general capabilities. Experimental results across diverse models show that our SafeSteer achieves a superior trade-off between safety and general capability compared with existing methods, attaining strong safety performance on seven safety benchmarks with only minimal degradation on five general capability benchmarks. Notably, SafeSteer requires only 100 harmful samples without using any general-purpose data, less than 1% of what previous baselines used, considerably reducing alignment cost. More details are on our project page at https://anjingkun.github.io/SafeSteer.
